correctness.rationale: The strict variance range places 0<c<m<b<L. For a two-point law at ℓ,h with mean m, the variance is (m−ℓ)(h−m); the mean fixes both weights. The two displayed laws therefore have the required moments. For a>0 the negative third derivative of exp(−ax) makes the quadratic Hermite interpolant at 0,b,b an upper bound and that at c,c,L a lower bound, with strictness off their nodes by the interpolation remainder on the full interval. Integrating quadratics uses only the common moments. The two transform bounds reverse for the pressure vector fields. Every field starts strictly positive, is strictly concave and eventually negative, so its unique positive root is strictly crossed and the solution increases to it. For strict finite-time comparisons, subtract the two ODEs and use an integrating factor: the forcing term is the positive pointwise difference of fields evaluated along the lower positive solution, and the divided-difference coefficient is bounded. At the smaller root the larger field is still positive, giving strict terminal comparison. Mixtures keep both moments, order the fields strictly at positive pressure and vary continuously at finite time and at the strictly crossed root, giving the full attainable intervals. The third centered moment for a two-point law is v(ℓ+h−2m); taking the difference gives Δ₃=vL(1−v/[m(L−m)]). As A(t)=τi₀t+O(t²), the first field-coefficient difference is τs₀Δ₃A³/6; integration gives exactly τ⁴s₀i₀³Δ₃t⁴/24+O(t⁵). The affine removed-proportion map preserves strict order. Jensen is strict for positive variance at positive pressure, and as L grows, the upper endpoint transform tends uniformly on bounded pressures to exp(−ma) because its interior atom tends to m and its remote atom has vanishing mass; solution and root continuity prove the uncapped comparison limit.
residual_risks: The finite verifier illustrations are not an all-time or all-laws proof. Endpoint uniqueness is for strictly positive initial infectives and interior variance; no stochastic finite-population, transmission-network, or peak ordering is asserted.

originality.rationale: The principal two-point moment laws and their Laplace order are classical bounded moment extremality. The scalar pressure model, homogeneous Jensen comparison, and unbounded two-moment final-size background are prior inputs; no novelty is credited to those. The supported distinct claim is the complete attainable interval in this fixed-cap, initially seeded scalar epidemic at every observation time and at infinity, including uniqueness and explicit sharp fourth-order opening. The cited model and moment theory combine to give weak envelope ordering, but the inspected statements do not give the full time-resolved attainment and onset coefficient. The strongest retrieved catalogue comparisons have different hypotheses and endpoints.
residual_risks: Katriel’s primary Theorems 3 and 6 and a precise passage in Karlin–Studden were not independently retrieved. An uninspected application of principal representations to exactly this seeded capped trajectory problem may materially bear on novelty; the verdict is limited to current evidence.

value.rationale: The capped-model conclusion turns an identifiability gap under two measured moments into an exact attainable observation-time interval, with common endpoint distributions and a quantitative order-of-onset separation. The fourth-order coefficient makes explicit when heterogeneity beyond the first two moments can affect pressure, and the cap limit quantifies the role of a hard support assumption. These are meaningful deterministic model comparisons, not claims about intervention or pathogen design.
residual_risks: The practical interpretation depends on a valid support cap and common model parameters. It is not a guarantee for finite stochastic outbreaks, uncertain initial conditions, or peaks.
